DrvStartRide.description: Start an NPC following a route, or wandering if the route is omitted.
DrvStartRide.note: Route paths are Data-relative. Acceptance may queue a ride while its model loads.

DrvStartRideTo.description: Send an NPC in a vehicle to a destination reference.
DrvStartRideTo.note: Use a placed destination reference. A successful request is not proof of arrival.

DrvStartChase.description: Ask an NPC driver to pursue a target reference.
DrvStartChase.note: The target may be a vehicle or actor.

DrvStopRide.note: retain motion: 0 stops the ride without retaining motion, 1 requests retaining motion.

DrvGetRideState.returns: 0 none, 1 pending, 2 route, 3 wander, 4 destination, 5 chasing.

DrvGetRideDriver.description: Read the driver assigned to an NPC ride.
DrvGetRideDriver.note: For a query that also covers the player, use vehicle.DrvGetVehicleDriver.

DrvGetRideTarget.description: Read an NPC ride’s chase target.

DrvSetRideSpeed.description: Change the cruise speed of an active NPC ride.
DrvSetRideSpeed.note: Speed is metres per second. Requires an active NPC driving session.

DrvSetRideAggression.description: Change the aggression value of an active NPC ride.
DrvSetRideAggression.note: Requires an active NPC driving session. The ride request default is 1.0.

DrvAddDriver.description: Spawn a driver at the calling vehicle and start a wandering ride.
DrvAddDriver.note: Call on the vehicle. The optional argument is an actor base, not an existing actor. If omitted, the traffic driver pool is used.

DrvStartEncounter.note: The quest must belong to a configured encounter.

DrvGetEncounterAlive.description: Count surviving members of a configured encounter.

DrvRepairVehicle.description: Restore vehicle health and supported damaged parts.
DrvRepairVehicle.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. This is a direct repair. It does not consume repair tools or apply the menu’s skill check. Active race service restrictions still apply.

DrvRefuel.description: Fill a vehicle’s configured fuel reserve.
DrvRefuel.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. This directly fills the reserve without consuming inventory supplies. Active race service restrictions still apply.

DrvGetVehicleHealth.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Use DrvGetVehicleCondition for a percentage.

DrvGetFuel.returns: Stored reserve in litres, or -1 for an invalid vehicle.
DrvGetFuel.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Use DrvGetFuelCapacity to check whether the vehicle has a supported fuel system.

DrvSetFuel.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. The value is litres, clamped to the vehicle’s capacity. No inventory supply is consumed.

DrvSpawnVehicle.note: Pass a base form, not a placed reference. The optional placement reference supplies position and heading. It falls back to the caller, then the player. Use an anchor in the player’s current world or cell. Arena unlock restrictions still apply.

DrvMount.description: Request mounting the player on a vehicle.
DrvMount.returns: 1 if the transition was requested, 0 otherwise.
DrvMount.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. This starts an action. It does not mean the transition has finished.

DrvRecoverVehicle.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Recovery can be refused by the vehicle’s current state or race restrictions.

DrvDamageVehicle.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Amount is raw health damage, not a percentage.

DrvPopTyre.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Use indices 0–5 for wheel slots. -1 punctures all slots. The vehicle must have an appropriate tyre rig for the expected visual result.

DrvSetVehicleLocked.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Use 0 to unlock, 1 to lock.

DrvSetHorseTack.description: Show or hide a horse’s tack.
DrvSetHorseTack.note: Use 0 to hide or 1 to show. Pass a horse reference or call on the horse.

DrvSetVehicleFault.description: Set a fault message which prevents normal use.
DrvSetVehicleFault.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. An empty string clears the fault.
DrvSetVehicleFault.example: DrvSetVehicleFault "The engine needs a replacement part." MyCarRef

DrvHasVehicleFault.description: Check whether a vehicle has a recorded fault.
DrvHasVehicleFault.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride.

DrvSetVehicleRestoration.description: Assign a restoration component and Repair requirement.
DrvSetVehicleRestoration.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. The component must be a MISC form. Repair skill must be between 0 and 100. Set a fault separately. This defines the requirement, it does not perform a repair.

DrvRestoreVehicle.description: Attempt the configured restoration using the player’s skill and inventory.
DrvRestoreVehicle.note: Pass a vehicle reference explicitly, or call on the vehicle / select it in the console. Omitting the argument does not automatically select your current ride. Requires the vehicle to be loaded, nearby, unlocked and unoccupied. On success the required item is consumed. This is separate from DrvRepairVehicle.

DrvStartRace.description: Queue race setup with optional vehicle assignments.
DrvStartRace.note: Omitted options use defaults. The opponent argument is a FormList of supported vehicle bases, up to 16 entries. This queues setup rather than confirming the race has begun.

DrvEndRace.description: Queue the end of the current race.

DrvHorseCrap.note: Choose a calm, stationary horse. Pass the horse, select it in the console, or omit the target while riding a horse.

IsDriving.description: Check whether an actor is driving.
IsDriving.note: Covers non-living vehicles, including stationary active driving sessions. IsRiding is the living-mount query.
IsDriving.example:
if Player.IsDriving
    let vehicle := DrvGetPlayerVehicle
endif

IsRiding.description: Check whether an actor is riding a horse or another living mount.
IsRiding.note: This is the living-mount query. IsDriving covers non-living vehicles. Use IsPassenger for passenger assignment.

DrvGetActorVehicle.description: Find an actor’s current vehicle or horse, including passengers.

DrvGetVehicleDriver.description: Get a vehicle’s active player or NPC driver.
DrvGetVehicleDriver.note: Pending NPC rides do not count as active drivers.

IsPassenger.description: Check whether an actor is assigned as a passenger.
IsPassenger.note: Reports logical seat assignment, including temporary save suspension.

IsInVehicle.description: Check whether an actor is aboard a specific vehicle.
IsInVehicle.returns: 1 if driver or passenger of that vehicle, otherwise 0.
IsInVehicle.example:
if Player.IsInVehicle MyCarRef
    let condition := MyCarRef.DrvGetVehicleCondition
endif

IsDrivable.description: Check whether a reference is a recognised vehicle or horse.

DrvGetVehicleType.returns: 0 invalid, 1 road, 2 motorcycle, 3 human-powered, 4 hover, 5 aircraft, 6 boat, 7 horse or living mount.

DrvGetPassengerCount.description: Count passengers assigned to this vehicle.
DrvGetPassengerCount.note: Passenger support concerns the player’s vehicle.

DrvGetPassenger.description: Get the passenger assigned to a seat.
DrvGetPassenger.note: Passenger seats start at 1. Query the driver separately.

DrvGetVehicleSpeed.description: Read horizontal speed, including reverse and sideways motion.
DrvGetVehicleSpeed.returns: Speed in metres per second, or -1 if unavailable.
DrvGetVehicleSpeed.note: Loaded parked vehicles return 0. Unloaded vehicles and untracked bumped hulls return -1. Multiply by 3.6 for km/h or 2.23694 for mph.

IsEngineRunning.description: Check whether a motorised engine is running.

IsVehicleOccupied.description: Check for an active driver or assigned passenger.

IsVehicleWrecked.description: Check for a destroyed hull or dead vehicle / mount.

DrvGetVehicleCondition.description: Read rounded vehicle health as a percentage.
DrvGetVehicleCondition.note: Use DrvGetVehicleHealth for raw health points.

DrvGetFuelCapacity.description: Read the capacity of a supported fuel system.
DrvGetFuelCapacity.returns: Capacity in litres, or -1 if unsupported.

CanUseVehicle.description: Check whether an actor can begin a fresh ride now.
CanUseVehicle.note: Does not reserve the vehicle or approve takeovers, theft confirmation or route availability. A later action can still fail.
CanUseVehicle.example:
if MyCarRef.CanUseVehicle Player
    DrvMount MyCarRef
endif

DrvGetVehicleUseFailure.description: Explain why an actor cannot begin a fresh ride.
DrvGetVehicleUseFailure.returns: 0 if allowed, otherwise a failure code from the table below.
DrvGetVehicleUseFailure.note: Uses the same eligibility check as CanUseVehicle.

IsStabled.description: Check whether a horse is registered in the stable.

DrvGetHorseCommand.returns: 0 free, 1 follow, 2 wait, or -1 if invalid.

DrvSetHorseCommand.description: Give a living stabled horse a command.
DrvSetHorseCommand.note: 0 free, 1 follow, 2 wait. Asking a new horse to follow moves the previous follower to wait.

DrvGetHorseTrait.description: Read one of the horse’s individual ratings.
DrvGetHorseTrait.note: Trait: 0 speed, 1 endurance, 2 nerve. Ratings are not physics multipliers.

DrvGetHorseStamina.note: Includes resting recovery. A profile with stamina disabled returns 100.

IsHorsePanicking.description: Check for active panic or a panic rear.

DrvSetHorseName.description: Rename a living player-owned stabled horse.
DrvSetHorseName.note: Accepts a string literal or string variable. Names are trimmed and limited to 31 allowed characters. An empty string restores the base name.

DrvSetHorseBond.description: Set a stabled horse’s bond for testing.
DrvSetHorseBond.note: Development console only. Requires a living, enabled, registered horse and a finite percentage from 0 to 100.

DrvPlaceRamp.description: Place a static ramp ahead of the player, aligned with their facing.
DrvPlaceRamp.note: Requires a STAT base. Placement uses terrain height where available. Check clearance yourself.
